document: EXHIBITION CONTRACT

This document evidences the Exhibition Contract (hereinafter the "Contract") entered into, on the one part, by the INSTITUTO DE INGENIEROS DE MINAS DEL PERÚ, with RUC 20107972090, with address at Calle Los Canarios 155-157, District of La Molina, Province and Department of Lima, duly represented by its General Manager, Mr. Gustavo Adolfo de Vinatea Bellatin, identified with DNI No. 07615912, with powers registered under Electronic File No. 11014857 of the Registry of Legal Entities of Lima, hereinafter referred to as IIMP; and, on the other part, {razon_social}, with RUC/RUT/TaxID, or equivalent No. {ruc}, with address at {domicilio_fiscal}, duly represented by {representante_legal}, identified with DNI/ identification card/ ID Card/Passport or other equivalent No. {dni_representante}, with powers registered under Electronic File No. {partida_electronica} of the Registry of Legal Entities of Lima (if applicable), hereinafter referred to simply as THE EXHIBITOR, in accordance with the particular terms set forth in this document and the General Exhibition Conditions of PERUMIN 38 and its Annexes.
IIMP and THE EXHIBITOR may be collectively referred to as THE PARTIES for purposes of this Contract.
FIRST: BACKGROUND

1.1 IIMP is an entity whose purpose is to convene and represent the professionals and companies related to mining activity in Peru. Its work is the promotion of mining activity in the country and the ongoing training of mining professionals, objectives that are achieved through international events such as the Mining Convention, among others.

1.2 IIMP is the organizer of PERUMIN 38 Mining Convention, an international event held every two years that it has organized since 1954 and that will take place in 2027 in the city of Arequipa, within the framework of which the Mining Technology Exhibition – EXTEMIN 2027 will be held, through the contracting of exhibition spaces (stands) intended for the presentation and promotion of its products, services, brands and activities, in accordance with the location, characteristics and conditions established in the Contract and its annexes.
3.  THE EXHIBITOR is {objeto_social}, whose purpose is to engage in {actividad}, and is interested in participating as an exhibitor in the EVENT under the terms set forth in this Contract.
SECOND: PURPOSE

By means of this Contract, IIMP grants to THE EXHIBITOR the temporary use of the exhibition module(s) identified in Annex 1 – Exhibition Modules and Location Plan, for its participation in the EXTEMIN 2027 Fair during the authorized periods of assembly, development of the EVENT and disassembly. As consideration, THE EXHIBITOR shall pay the amount and at the times established in Annex 2 – Form and Payment Conditions.
This assignment does not create any right of possession, usufruct or permanent commercial lease, but only a temporary right of use for the purposes of the EVENT.
THIRD: INTEGRAL DOCUMENTS
The following form an integral part of the contracting:
a)  This Exhibition Contract.
b)  The General Exhibition Conditions of PERUMIN 38.
c)  Annex 1 – Exhibition Modules and Location Plan.
d)  Annex 2 – Economic Conditions and Payment Schedule.
e)  Annex 3 – Exhibitor's Compliance Statement
f)  Annex 4 – Exhibitors' Regulations.
g) Annex 5 – Participation Regulations
FOURTH: ACCEPTANCE OF THE GENERAL CONDITIONS

By executing this Contract, THE EXHIBITOR declares that it has received, reviewed and fully accepted the General Exhibition Conditions of PERUMIN 38, which form an integral part of the contracting and are mandatory.

Acceptance of the General Conditions is made in full and without reservations. Any annotation, reservation or condition unilaterally incorporated by THE EXHIBITOR shall be deemed not made and shall have no effect against IIMP.
Gustavo Adolfo De Vinatea Bellatin
General Manager
IIMP THE EXHIBITOR
GENERAL EXHIBITION CONDITIONS
PERUMIN 38
FIRST: SCOPE AND APPLICATION

These General Conditions govern the rights, obligations and rules applicable to THE EXHIBITOR's participation in PERUMIN 38 Mining Convention (hereinafter, the EVENT), and form an integral part of the Exhibition Contract.

The particular conditions of each contracting, including the exhibition module(s) assigned, the consideration and the payment schedule, shall be established exclusively in the Contract and its annexes.

The Contract and its annexes specify such particular conditions and do not modify these General Conditions. Any annotation, reservation or condition unilaterally incorporated by THE EXHIBITOR shall be deemed not made and shall have no effect against IIMP.
SECOND: DEFINITIONS

For purposes of these General Conditions, EVENT shall mean PERUMIN 38 Mining Convention, to be held in the city of Arequipa, from September 20 to 24, 2027, at the Cerro Juli Convention Center, including the EXTEMIN Fair and other official and complementary activities; module or exhibition space shall mean the physical space identified in Annex 1 granted in temporary use to THE EXHIBITOR; Exhibitors' Regulations shall mean the technical, operational and conduct provisions contained in Annex 4, applicable to THE EXHIBITOR; and Participation Regulations, contained in Annex 5, shall mean the accreditation, credentials, entry, stay, conduct and security provisions applicable to THE EXHIBITOR's personnel, representatives, suppliers and guests who participate in or attend the EVENT.
THIRD: OBLIGATIONS OF THE PARTIES
3.1 By IIMP:
3.1.1 Deliver the exhibition space on the date scheduled for assembly, according to the plan approved in Annex 1.
3.1.2 Provide exclusively the basic technical facilities expressly set forth in the Exhibitors' Regulations.
3.1.3  Comply with its obligations as organizer of the EVENT in matters of safety and health, in accordance with applicable regulations.
3.2 By THE EXHIBITOR:

3.2.1  Pay the consideration established in Annex 2 in a timely manner. Delay in any of the payments shall entitle IIMP to suspend delivery of the space and the benefits pending performance until the total regularization of the amounts owed, without such suspension constituting a breach attributable to IIMP or giving rise to any right to refund, compensation or extension of benefits.
3.2.2 Respect the provisions of the Exhibitors' Regulations, the assembly and disassembly schedules, and the safety rules of the EVENT.
3.2.3 Use the exhibition space solely for the purposes of the EVENT, without assigning or transferring it to third parties.
3.2.4  Keep its stand orderly and clean, assuming liability for any damages that its employees, representatives or contractors may cause.
3.2.5  Comply with IIMP's institutional policies on integrity, sustainability and regulatory compliance.

3.2.6 Confirm each payment by email addressed to cobranzas@iimp.org.pe, attaching the corresponding bank receipt and stating, as reference, the number of the invoice issued by IIMP, and THE EXHIBITOR's corporate name and RUC

3.2.7 Submit to IIMP, within the term established in the Exhibitors' Regulations, the stand design and technical plans, by email addressed to {correo_planos}, for verification of compliance with the operational and safety conditions of the EVENT.

3.2.8 Review and approve, under its responsibility, the final stand design before authorizing its manufacture, construction or assembly. Any review carried out by IIMP does not replace such approval nor imply the assumption of liability for design or execution errors.
3.2.9 Obtain and keep in force the licenses, permits, insurance and authorizations required for the construction, installation, operation and disassembly of the stand.

3.2.10 Verify the location, dimensions and visible conditions of the space at the time of delivery, recording any observation before starting assembly. Commencement of assembly without observations shall constitute acceptance of the visible conditions of the space received.
3.2.11 Remedy, at its own expense and cost, the observations, deficiencies or technical and safety breaches relating to its stand, within the term indicated by IIMP.

3.2.12 Completely remove, within the established term, the stand, equipment, materials and other goods brought into the EVENT, and repair any damage caused to the venue or to third parties by its activities.

3.2.13 Be liable for the acts, omissions, errors, breaches and damages caused by its suppliers and contractors, even when these have been registered, authorized or approved by IIMP. Such approval does not constitute a guarantee nor create liability for IIMP for the services contracted by THE EXHIBITOR.
3.2.14 Sign the delivery and return records of the exhibition space, stating its condition, any existing observations and, where applicable, pending damages or repairs.
FOURTH: INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY

It is expressly established that this Contract does not imply any assignment of rights or ownership in favor of IIMP with respect to the distinctive signs owned by THE EXHIBITOR, who retains ownership thereof.

THE EXHIBITOR declares that all materials, products, demonstrations, images, trademarks and promotional content exhibited or distributed at its stand are owned by it, have the corresponding authorizations or are duly licensed, and do not infringe third-party intellectual property rights.
FIFTH: USE AND LIMITATION OF THE BRAND AND OF THE EXHIBITORS' REGULATIONS
5.1 Use of the EVENT brand is limited to stand identification, without external promotional purposes, and shall require prior written authorization from IIMP for any other use.

5.2 THE EXHIBITOR undertakes not to make structural modifications or unauthorized installations at the stand, and the exhibition of flammable material or material contrary to safety rules and institutional ethics is prohibited.

5.3 The Exhibitors' Regulations form an integral part of this Contract as Annex 4. Breach thereof may result in a warning, temporary suspension of benefits or, in the event of a serious or repeated infringement, resolution of the Contract in accordance with Clause Thirteen.

5.4 IIMP reserves the right to prevent the entry or assembly of stands, modules or exhibition structures when THE EXHIBITOR has not paid the total consideration or has breached the Regulations, without this giving rise to liability for IIMP.

5.5 Improper use of the brand shall entitle IIMP to order the immediate removal of the material and, where it constitutes a material breach, to resolve the Contract in accordance with Clause Thirteen.
SIXTH: ASSIGNMENT OF RIGHTS

THE EXHIBITOR may not assign or transfer under any title its right to use the exhibition space, or its contractual position, without the prior written authorization of IIMP, which may be denied without need for justification.
SEVENTH: TERM
This Contract shall enter into force upon its execution and shall end upon the total removal of THE EXHIBITOR's stand and equipment, in accordance with the official schedule of the EVENT.
EIGHTH: SPECIFIC UNDERTAKINGS OF THE EXHIBITOR AND APPROVAL OF SUPPLIERS

8.1 THE EXHIBITOR undertakes to prepare an exhibition of materials, equipment, machinery, supplies or services related to the activities of the EVENT, which must have the prior approval of IIMP and be strictly consistent with the Exhibitors' Regulations.

8.2 THE EXHIBITOR undertakes to comply with the supplier approval procedure applied by IIMP for stand construction, catering, logistics operations, assembly, maintenance and other related services. In the event it engages a construction or assembly company, the latter must necessarily go through such approval process.

8.3 THE EXHIBITOR shall be solely responsible for the engagement, supervision and performance of the obligations of its suppliers or contractors, even when these are approved by IIMP, and IIMP shall not assume any liability for their breach, deficiency or damages arising from such services. The approval, registration or authorization of a supplier by IIMP does not constitute a recommendation, quality guarantee or assumption of liability for the services such supplier provides to THE EXHIBITOR. The contractual relationship shall be maintained exclusively between THE EXHIBITOR and its supplier.

8.4 THE EXHIBITOR shall comply with the current safety, health and environmental regulations applicable during the assembly, operation and disassembly of its module, including the provisions of the Ministry of Health, Civil Defense and other competent authorities, as well as the measures established by IIMP or the venue administration.

8.5 THE EXHIBITOR shall be responsible for managing the access of its communication, photography or filming crews as part of its personnel, which shall not be considered press and whose entry shall be subject to the protocols of the EVENT organization.

8.6 THE EXHIBITOR shall be responsible for the suitability of the content and of the human or material resources used for its production (including influencers, opinion leaders, politicians or others). IIMP reserves the right to request the removal of THE EXHIBITOR's brand or the suspension of its participation when the content or messages disseminated are contrary to ethics, current regulations or IIMP's institutional values.

8.7 If THE EXHIBITOR does not occupy the assigned module or space within the term established in the Exhibitors' Regulations, it shall automatically lose the right to occupy it, and IIMP shall be entitled to reassign it to another exhibitor or use it for institutional purposes, with no obligation of refund or indemnification. Failure to occupy within the indicated terms shall be considered tacit withdrawal, and the penalties set forth in Clause Thirteen shall apply.
NINTH: SUSTAINABILITY, ETHICS AND SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY COMMITMENT (ESG)

THE EXHIBITOR undertakes to carry out its participation in the EVENT respecting principles of environmental sustainability, social responsibility and ethical conduct, in accordance with respect for human rights and good social and legal practices, avoiding any practice that may negatively affect the image or institutional values of IIMP, or constitute discrimination, corruption or an act contrary to public order.

This commitment includes the responsible use of materials, the promotion of appropriate institutional messages, respect for current environmental and social regulations, and compliance with IIMP's institutional policies on integrity and ethics, ensuring that its representatives and contractors maintain conduct consistent with such principles.
TENTH: PREVENTION OF MONEY LAUNDERING AND TERRORISM FINANCING

10.1 THE PARTIES declare that the funds and resources used under this Contract have a lawful origin and undertake to comply with the applicable national and international regulations on the prevention of money laundering and terrorism financing.

10.2 THE EXHIBITOR declares that neither it nor, to the best of its knowledge and belief, its beneficial owners or legal representatives are included in binding lists applicable in Peru related to money laundering, terrorism financing or financing of the proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.

10.3 THE EXHIBITOR declares that all information and documentation provided to IIMP in connection with the contracting is complete, truthful and current. It also undertakes to notify any relevant change in such information that could materially affect the contractual relationship.

10.4 THE PARTIES undertake to notify each other, within five (5) business days of becoming aware, of any investigation, final sanction or inclusion in a binding list that could affect their reputation or the performance of this Contract. This obligation does not include information that, under applicable law, is confidential or whose disclosure is prohibited.

10.5 The submission of false information, the omission of relevant information or the material and proven breach of the obligations set forth in this clause shall constitute a material breach and shall entitle the non-breaching party to resolve the Contract in accordance with Clause Thirteen.
ELEVENTH: ANTI-CORRUPTION AND INTEGRITY

11.1 THE PARTIES undertake to comply with the applicable Peruvian legislation on integrity, prevention and punishment of corruption, including Law No. 30424, its Regulations and amending rules, as well as OECD standards and other ethical principles applicable to international events. Likewise, each party shall comply with the foreign rules legally applicable to it by reason of its incorporation or activities.

11.2 THE PARTIES shall refrain from offering, promising, authorizing, giving, requesting or accepting, directly or indirectly, improper payments, gifts, benefits or advantages intended to influence commercial, contractual, administrative or public decisions related to this Contract. It is prohibited to use the contracting to conceal, facilitate or carry out acts of bribery, influence peddling, fraud, collusion, private corruption or any other unlawful practice.

11.3 The obligations set forth in this clause extend to the directors, officers, employees, representatives, agents and subcontractors acting on behalf of or under the control of each party in activities related to the performance of this Contract. Each party shall adopt reasonable measures to prevent such persons from engaging in the prohibited conduct.
11.4 THE PARTIES undertake to timely notify any conflict of interest or connection with public officials that may directly affect the decisions or activities related to this Contract.

11.5 When there are objective indications of a possible breach of this clause, the affected party may request information or documentation reasonably related to the identified facts. The request shall respect confidentiality, personal data protection, professional secrecy and other applicable legal reservations.

11.6 The material and proven breach of this clause shall constitute a material breach and shall entitle the non-breaching party to suspend or resolve the Contract in accordance with Clause Thirteen, without prejudice to reporting the facts to the competent authorities where appropriate.
TWELFTH: LIABILITY, INDEMNITY AND INSURANCE

12.1 Each party shall be liable for the direct, certain and duly evidenced damages caused to the other as an immediate consequence of the non-performance or the partial, late or defective performance of the obligations directly incumbent upon it, provided that such breach is attributable to it under applicable law.

12.2 THE EXHIBITOR shall be liable for damages to persons, property or facilities caused by its representatives, contractors or suppliers, as well as for its own activities within the EVENT. Consequently, it shall hold IIMP harmless from third-party claims, sanctions, damages or contingencies that are a direct consequence of such acts or omissions or of the breach of its obligations. IIMP shall timely notify THE EXHIBITOR of any claim or proceeding and allow it to participate in its handling or defense.

12.3 THE EXHIBITOR shall take out, at its own expense, civil liability insurance in force during the assembly, development and disassembly of the EVENT, covering damages to persons, property or facilities arising from its participation.

12.4 IIMP shall hold THE EXHIBITOR harmless only from third-party claims that are the direct and proven consequence of the breach of the organization obligations expressly assumed by IIMP. In the event of damages attributable to IIMP's personnel or suppliers, liability shall be assessed in accordance with the applicable legislation and coverage, and IIMP shall be liable only in the case of proven negligence, without this implying automatic acknowledgment of liability or indemnification.

12.5 THE EXHIBITOR shall be responsible for the custody and security of the equipment, materials, products, personal belongings and other goods it brings into the EVENT. IIMP shall not act as depositary nor be liable for their loss, theft, misappropriation or deterioration, unless it is proven that the damage was a direct consequence of a breach attributable to IIMP with respect to a custody or security obligation expressly assumed in the Contract. The provision of general security and surveillance services for the EVENT does not imply that IIMP assumes individual custody of THE EXHIBITOR's goods.

12.6 IIMP shall not be liable for delays, failures, interruptions, damages or breaches caused by suppliers, contractors or third parties directly engaged by THE EXHIBITOR, nor for instructions, materials, information or content provided by the latter.
THIRTEENTH: RESOLUTION, WITHDRAWAL AND TERMINATION OF THE CONTRACT
13.1 Resolution for material breach
This Contract may be resolved by operation of law, in accordance with Article 1430 of the Civil Code, when either of THE PARTIES breaches the following material obligations:
a) On the part of THE EXHIBITOR:
i.  Pay the consideration or any of its installments in the amounts and within the terms established in Annex 2.

ii.  Improperly use, alter or distort the name, trademarks, logos or image of IIMP or of the EVENT, including their use by allies, media or third parties for purposes other than those authorized or for its own benefit.
iii.  Use or disseminate IIMP's brand, materials or content for commercial, advertising or covert marketing purposes that may mislead or cause confusion.
iv.  Assign the exhibition space without authorization or breach the Exhibitors' Regulations.
v.  Seriously breach the conduct, integrity or safety rules established by IIMP, when such breach affects institutional reputation, the safety of the EVENT or compliance with applicable regulations.
vi.  Comply with the obligations set forth in Clauses Ten and Eleven.
b) On the part of IIMP:
i.  Fail to grant the exhibition space or the services specifically contracted, under the conditions and at the times agreed.
ii.  Use without authorization, alter or distort the name, trademarks, logos or image of THE EXHIBITOR.
iii.  Substantially and unjustifiably modify the agreed conditions, preventing the exercise of THE EXHIBITOR's rights.
13.2 Cure and notice of resolution

When the breach is capable of cure, the affected party shall request its correction in writing, granting a term of five (5) business days. When the proximity of the EVENT does not allow such term to be observed, a shorter term may be granted, reasonably determined based on the circumstances.

It shall not be necessary to grant a cure period when: (a) non-payment occurs upon the deadline established to participate in the EVENT; (b) a breach in matters of money laundering, terrorism financing, corruption or integrity which, by its nature, is not capable of cure; (c) an unauthorized use of trademarks that causes or may cause immediate damage; or (d) a breach that makes it impossible to perform the obligation before or during the EVENT.

The resolution shall occur by operation of law when the affected party notifies the breaching party in writing of its decision to enforce this termination clause, identifying the material obligation breached.
13.3 Effects of resolution attributable to THE EXHIBITOR

In the event of resolution for reasons attributable to THE EXHIBITOR: (a) it shall lose the right to occupy the space and to pending services; (b) IIMP may retain thirty percent (30%) of the total consideration as a penalty; (c) IIMP shall additionally retain the amounts corresponding to the benefits effectively granted and to the direct, non-recoverable and duly evidenced expenses incurred to perform THE EXHIBITOR's particular obligations; (d) the penalty may be offset against the amounts paid by THE EXHIBITOR, and if these are insufficient, THE EXHIBITOR shall pay the difference within ten (10) business days following the corresponding notice; and (e) if there is a balance in favor of THE EXHIBITOR after the settlement, IIMP shall return it, without interest, within the following thirty (30) calendar days. The sum of the penalty, services effectively rendered and costs of reservation, preparation and provision of the space and the recognized expenses may not exceed the total value of the Contract.
13.4 Effects of resolution attributable to IIMP

In the event of resolution for reasons attributable to IIMP, the amounts corresponding to the rights of use of the space and contracted services shall be returned to THE EXHIBITOR within a maximum term of forty-five (45) calendar days counted from the notification of the resolution, without interest.
13.5 Withdrawal by THE EXHIBITOR

THE EXHIBITOR may notify in writing its decision to withdraw from its participation in the EVENT. Such notice does not exempt it from payment of the amounts already invoiced and shall give rise to the application of the following penalties on the total amount of the Contract, according to the date of notice:
Date of notice of withdrawal
Penalty applicable on the total amount of the Contract
From December 1, 2026 to January 31, 2027
From February 1 to April 30, 2027
From May 1 to July 31, 2027
From August 1, 2027 or later
100% (no refund whatsoever)

These penalties compensate the administrative, logistical and promotional expenses assumed by IIMP, without prejudice to its right to dispose of the contracted space again. Likewise, THE EXHIBITOR shall assume an administrative penalty equal to ten percent (10%) of the total contracted amount when it requests a change in the location of its module or a change of corporate name or contractual holder, unless such change is due to a corporate reorganization or a duly justified cause that does not cause harm to IIMP. IIMP may deduct the established penalties from the amounts paid by THE EXHIBITOR, without requiring any additional procedure or express authorization.
This numeral shall not apply when, at the time of notifying the withdrawal, THE EXHIBITOR is in breach of a material obligation, in which case the effects set forth in numeral 13.3 shall apply.
13.6 Termination by mutual agreement

THE PARTIES may terminate this Contract at any time by written document signed by their duly authorized representatives, which shall establish the economic consequences, performed obligations and pending obligations arising from the termination.
FOURTEENTH: FORTUITOUS EVENT OR FORCE MAJEURE

Neither of THE PARTIES shall be liable for the breach of its obligations when such breach is a direct consequence of a fortuitous event or force majeure, understood as any extraordinary, unforeseeable and irresistible event, in accordance with Article 1315 of the Civil Code. Such events include, by way of example and not limitation, natural disasters, social conflicts, acts of authority, pandemics, general strikes or any other event beyond the reasonable control of the affected party.

The affected party shall notify the other in writing, within a reasonable term, of the occurrence of the event and its impact on the performance of contractual obligations. During the continuance of the force majeure event, the obligations shall be suspended without liability for the parties.

If the fortuitous event or force majeure makes it impossible to hold the EVENT on the scheduled date, its rescheduling and the corresponding economic consequences shall be governed by Clause Fifteen. If the situation persists and makes performance of the Contract impossible, THE PARTIES may agree to reschedule it or, ultimately, to resolve it without penalty.
FIFTEENTH: POSTPONEMENT OF THE EVENT

In the event the EVENT is postponed or moved to a new location, IIMP shall notify such decision to THE EXHIBITOR with reasonable advance notice, not less than thirty (30) calendar days, except in the case of force majeure or fortuitous event.

Amounts previously paid shall be applied to the new date or venue of the EVENT, and the agreed rights and benefits shall remain in force. However, if the postponement exceeds twelve (12) months, the EVENT is moved to another city, or it is not possible to maintain or replace the main benefits with others of equivalent value, THE EXHIBITOR may request termination of the Contract within ten (10) business days following the notice. In such case, IIMP shall return the amounts corresponding to the benefits not performed, deducting the benefits already granted and, where the postponement or relocation is due to causes not attributable to IIMP, the direct, non-recoverable and duly evidenced costs.
SIXTEENTH: TAXES

All taxes arising as a consequence of the execution and performance of this Contract shall be assumed by THE PARTIES as applicable, in accordance with applicable laws. The payment receipts issued by IIMP shall comply with the deductibility requirements set forth in current tax regulations, recognizing THE EXHIBITOR's right to apply the withholdings or advance payments required by law.
SEVENTEENTH: PERSONAL DATA PROTECTION

In the event that, for the performance of this Contract, either of THE PARTIES accesses personal data of the other or of third parties, it undertakes to process them in accordance with Law No. 29733 and its Regulations, using them solely for purposes related to the EVENT and maintaining their confidentiality even after the end of the Contract, except for a legal obligation of disclosure.

When the performance of the Contract requires the provision of personal data of third parties, the party collecting them must have the express authorization of their owners, ensuring that their processing is limited to the aforementioned purposes. THE EXHIBITOR also authorizes the use of its trade name, trademark and logo exclusively for the performance and dissemination of its participation in PERUMIN 38.
EIGHTEENTH: NOTICES

THE PARTIES agree that the notices and communications arising from this Contract shall be considered validly made when effected at the address indicated by each party in the Contract. Likewise, communications sent to the institutional email declared by each party shall be fully valid and produce all their effects, being deemed made on the date of their sending.

In the case of exhibitors from the provinces or abroad, the address or legal representative designated in Lima or, failing that, the electronic address registered in the Contract shall be considered valid.
NINETEENTH: SUPPLEMENTARY APPLICATION
For all matters not regulated in this Contract, THE PARTIES submit to the supplementary application of the Civil Code of Peru and other applicable rules.
TWENTIETH: JURISDICTION AND ADDRESSES

For purposes of any dispute arising from the execution and performance of this Contract, THE PARTIES submit to the territorial jurisdiction of the judges and courts of the district of Cercado de Lima, waiving in advance the venue of their domicile.

The review, conformity or approval carried out by IIMP shall be solely intended to verify compliance with the operational, technical and safety provisions of the EVENT, and shall not constitute approval of the quality, functionality, stability, dimensions, finishes or suitability of the design for THE EXHIBITOR's needs.

3.1 Our services are subject to the General Sales Tax (IGV) in accordance with current tax regulations, as they are rendered within Peruvian territory. For foreign clients, IIMP shall issue the corresponding electronic receipt, in accordance with the applicable tax regime and SUNAT provisions.

3.2 Detraction: The temporary assignment of the exhibition space is subject to the Tax Obligations Payment System – SPOT, in accordance with current tax regulations. Consequently, THE EXHIBITOR shall deposit ten percent (10%) of the amount of the invoice issued by IIMP into IIMP's detraction account at Banco de la Nación (Soles Account No. 000-00-372668) and timely send the corresponding receipt. Failing that, it shall pay the total value of the invoice so that IIMP performs the corresponding self-detraction.

5. Invoicing Instructions

THE EXHIBITOR shall previously provide its complete and correct data for the issuance of the payment receipt (corporate name, RUC or equivalent, fiscal address and email). IIMP shall issue the receipts in accordance with the payment schedule and current tax regulations. If it requires the modification or change of the type of receipt issued, THE EXHIBITOR may request it within a maximum term of ten (10) business days counted from the date of receipt of the electronic receipt; after such term, modification requests shall not be accepted.
6. Payment Confirmation
